title: Thouless Pumping of One-Dimensional Dark Solitons and Domain Walls
authors: Fangwei Ye, Aidar H. Ryazhapov, Yaroslav V. Kartashov, Vladimir V. Konotop
abstract: We predict that quantized transport of dark solitons and domain walls can be observed in mutually sliding optical lattices in both focusing and defocusing nonlinear materials. Two different classes of underlying periodic backgrounds are considered here -- unstaggered and staggered -- which are accurately represented, respectively, by the in-phase and out-of-phase trains of Wannier functions. The nonlinear excitations formed on top of these backgrounds -- dark solitons and domain walls -- are sustained by defocusing or focusing Kerr nonlinearities of the optical medium. Despite non-zero asymptotics, dark solitons and domain walls can still undergo quantized topological transport in dynamically changing refractive index landscape when they and background on which they are constructed are dynamically stable. The extended intervals of propagation constants (and, correspondingly, of the background amplitude) and lattice depths, where stable quantized transport occurs, are identified for both dark solitons and domain walls. Outside these intervals, the quantized transport regime is found to be unstable. Our results extend the concept of nonlinear topological transport from bright to dark soliton states.
summary: This theoretical study predicts and analyzes the quantized transport of dark solitons and domain walls within dynamically changing optical lattices. By extending the concept of Thouless pumping to dark excitations, the authors map out the parameter regimes where stable, topologically protected transport can occur in both focusing and defocusing nonlinear media.
main_problem: The paper investigates the quantized transport, known as Thouless Pumping, of one-dimensional dark solitons and domain walls.
main_result: Quantized topological transport can be observed for both dark solitons and domain walls in mutually sliding optical lattices, extending the concept from bright to dark soliton states.
method: The analysis uses perturbation theory in the adiabatic limit, expanding solutions in slow variables, and analyzing the center of mass shift over pumping cycles.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the nonlinear Schrödinger equation describing light propagation in a periodic potential created by two mutually sliding optical lattices. The excitations studied are dark solitons and domain walls.
key_observables: Quantized topological transport (quantized shift in center of mass, $\delta x_c$), stability of pumping, and the background amplitude/propagation constant ($b$).
important_parameters: The nonlinearity ($\chi$), the lattice depths, the propagation constant ($b$), and the adiabatic parameter ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the adiabatic limit ($\alpha \ll 1$), and the Wannier function expansion is assumed accurate.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate examples of modulated backgrounds (unstaggered/staggered) and show the evolution of the center of mass shift ($\delta x_c$) for both stable and unstable pumping regimes for solitons and domain walls.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model using the NSE, analyzes the background structure (unstaggered vs. staggered), develops the adiabatic perturbation theory, and finally presents the results showing the quantized transport and identifying the stable parameter regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges nonlinear wave physics (solitons) with topological concepts (Thouless pumping), providing a detailed theoretical framework for observing quantized effects in optical systems, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and nonlinear dynamics.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Modulated unstaggered background in a defocusing medium at b = 9.0 (belonging to the first finite gap in spectrum of R) (a) and staggered background in a focusing medium at b = 11.5 (belonging to the semi-infinite gap in spectrum of R). Black lines show exact solutions, while red lines show the reconstructed background from Wannier functions from the first band. Dashed violet line schematically shows the profile of the lattice R at z = 0. In all cases p1,2 = 8, d1 = 1, d2 = 2.

Figure 2: Amplitude of dark soliton (open circles) and domain wall (red triangles) vs propagation constant b in defocusing (a) and focusing (d) media, obtained for z = 0. Gray areas correspond to allowed bands. Inside the forbidden gap, the families of dark solitons and domain walls are practically non-distinguishable on the scale of the figures. Profiles of unstaggered dark soliton (b) and domain wall (c) with b = 9 in a defocusing medium. Profiles of staggered dark soliton (e), and domain wall (f) with b = 11.5 in a focusing medium. Dashed violet line schematically shows the profile of the lattice R at z = 0. In all cases p1,2 = 8, d1 = 1, d2 = 2.

Figure 3: Stable Thouless pumping of unstaggered dark soliton with b = 8.0 (a) and domain wall with b = 9.0 (b) in defocusing medium, and of staggered dark soliton (c) and domain wall (d) with b = 11.5 in focusing medium. Unstable pumping leading to decay of (e) unstaggered dark soliton with b = 9.3 in defocusing medium and (f) staggered domain wall with b = 10.9 in focusing medium. Top row shows dynamics of |Ψ| in the (x, z) plane, bottom row shows displacement of center of mass δxc vs distance z. Three pumping cycles are shown in panels (a)-(d) with stable dynamics, and only one cycle is shown in panels (e),(f) showing unstable pumping. Sliding velocity of sublattices is α = 0.001.

Figure 4: Displacement of the center of solution over one pumping cycle versus propagation constant b for unstaggered dark soliton (a) and domain wall (b) at p1,2 = 8 in defocusing medium. White regions show domain of stable pumping, gray regions—of unstable pumping. Vertical blue dashed lines show borders of the first finite gap.

Figure 5: Stable pumping domains on the (p1,2, b) plane for unstaggered dark solitons (a) and domain walls (b) in defocusing medium, and for staggered dark solitons (c) and domain walls (d) in focusing medium. Stable pumping occurs between open and solid blue dots. Gray regions show allowed bands at z = 0. Stars show the border of soliton existence domain. In all cases sliding velocity α = 0.001.
